question: Which of the following digital programmes aims to make the legislative proceedings of the State and Union Territory Legislatures in India completely paperless? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: e-Governance for Legislators (eGL)
Digital India Mission
e-Parliament
National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA)

Explanation:
The National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA) is a digital programme of the Government of India aimed at making the legislative proceedings of State and Union Territory Legislatures completely paperless. It facilitates the digital presentation and distribution of legislative documents such as bills, questions, notices, and other papers. NeVA is being implemented by the Ministry of Home Affairs and is a part of the Digital India Mission. Its primary objectives include enhancing transparency, reducing paper consumption, and making the legislative process more efficient. Several state legislatures have already adopted this application.

question: In India, the area under 'Permanent Pastures and Grazing Lands' is mostly owned by: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: cooperatives
private companies
the Forest Department
Village Panchayats
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Village Panchayats

Explanation:
In India, most of the area under permanent pastures and grazing lands is owned by Village Panchayats. These lands are considered community resources used by villagers for grazing livestock and other collective purposes. According to Indian land use statistics, these lands are classified in revenue records and are managed by local Gram Panchayats, which have the authority over their usage. This is distinctly different from ownership by private companies, cooperatives, or the Forest Department. The community-based ownership ensures sustainable management and access for rural populations.

question: Who has the authority to transfer judges of the High Courts in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: President of India
Chief Minister of the State
Parliament of India
Chief Justice of India acting on behalf of the Supreme Court
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President of India

Explanation:
According to Article 222 of the Indian Constitution, the authority to transfer judges of the High Courts lies with the President of India. This power is exercised after consulting the Chief Justice of India (CJI). Although the CJI's advice is not binding, consultation is mandatory to maintain judicial independence. The President can transfer any judge from one High Court to another without the judge's consent. This provision ensures the efficient functioning of the judiciary while balancing executive power with judicial consultation. The transfer process is a key feature of India's federal judicial system, allowing flexibility and optimal utilization of judicial resources across states. The President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, but in this matter, the consultation with the CJI is a crucial safeguard.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who has the power to transfer High Court judges? → President of India
☛ Who must be consulted before such transfer? → Chief Justice of India
☛ Which article deals with transfer of High Court judges? → Article 222
☛ Is the CJI's advice binding on the President? → No
☛ Can a judge be transferred without consent? → Yes
question_hi: भारत में उच्च न्यायालयों के न्यायाधीशों का स्थानांतरण करने का अधिकार किसके पास है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 1)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत के राष्ट्रपति

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 222 के अनुसार, उच्च न्यायालयों के न्यायाधीशों का स्थानांतरण राष्ट्रपति द्वारा किया जाता है। यह अधिकार राष्ट्रपति को भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश (CJI) से परामर्श करने के बाद प्राप्त होता है। हालांकि, मुख्य न्यायाधीश की सलाह बाध्यकारी नहीं है, लेकिन न्यायिक स्वतंत्रता बनाए रखने के लिए परामर्श अनिवार्य है। यह प्रावधान न्यायाधीशों के हस्तांतरण को नियंत्रित करता है, जिससे न्यायपालिका की स्वायत्तता और कार्यक्षमता सुनिश्चित होती है। राष्ट्रपति किसी भी उच्च न्यायालय के किसी न्यायाधीश को उसकी सहमति के बिना किसी अन्य उच्च न्यायालय में स्थानांतरित कर सकते हैं। यह शक्ति संविधान के तहत कार्यपालिका को दी गई है, लेकिन न्यायिक हस्तक्षेप और परामर्श की प्रक्रिया से संतुलित की गई है।

question: Which of the following constitutional bodies was created to recommend appointments and transfers of judges in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: National Judicial Appointments Commission
High Court Tribunal
Supreme Council of Judges
Central Judicial Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC)

Explanation:
The National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) was created by the 99th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2014 to recommend appointments and transfers of judges in India. It was intended to replace the collegium system. NJAC consisted of six members: the Chief Justice of India, two senior-most Supreme Court judges, the Union Law Minister, and two eminent persons. It made recommendations for the appointment of judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts. However, in October 2015, the Supreme Court declared the NJAC Act and the 99th Amendment unconstitutional, restoring the collegium system. The objective of NJAC was to bring greater transparency and accountability in judicial appointments.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which amendment created NJAC? → 99th Constitutional Amendment, 2014
☛ How many members were in NJAC? → 6
☛ In which year was NJAC declared unconstitutional? → 2015
☛ Which system replaced NJAC? → Collegium system
☛ Who recommends appointments in the collegium system? → Senior Supreme Court judges

question: The provision of early childhood care and education to children below six years of age was introduced by which Constitutional Amendment? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Forty-second Amendment Act, 1976
Seventy-fourth Amendment Act, 1992
Eighty-sixth Amendment Act, 2002
Forty-fourth Amendment Act, 1978
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Eighty-sixth Amendment Act, 2002

Explanation:
The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 was enacted to make education a fundamental right in India. It inserted Article 21A, providing free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14 years. It also amended Article 45, directing the state to endeavor to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years. Additionally, a new fundamental duty (Clause K) was added under Article 51A, imposing a duty on parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6 to 14. This amendment was a landmark step towards ensuring universal access to education and laying the foundation for the Right to Education Act, 2009.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which amendment made education a fundamental right? → 86th Amendment, 2002
☛ Article 21A deals with? → Free education for 6-14 years
☛ What does Article 45 provide? → Early childhood care for children below 6 years
☛ Which fundamental duty was added by 86th Amendment? → Article 51A, Clause K
☛ When did the 86th Amendment come into force? → 1 April, 2010
question_hi: छह वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों को प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखभाल और शिक्षा का प्रावधान किस संवैधानिक संशोधन द्वारा पेश किया गया था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: बयालीसवां संशोधन अधिनियम, 1976
चौहत्तरवां संशोधन अधिनियम, 1992
छियासीवां संशोधन अधिनियम, 2002
चौवालीसवां संशोधन अधिनियम, 1978
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है छियासीवां संशोधन अधिनियम, 2002

Explanation:
86वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2002 भारतीय संविधान में शिक्षा के अधिकार को मौलिक अधिकार बनाने के लिए लाया गया था। इसने अनुच्छेद 21A जोड़ा, जो 6 से 14 वर्ष के बच्चों को मुफ्त और अनिवार्य शिक्षा प्रदान करता है। साथ ही, इसने अनुच्छेद 45 में संशोधन करके राज्य को निर्देशित किया कि वह सभी बच्चों को छह वर्ष की आयु पूरी करने तक प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखभाल और शिक्षा प्रदान करने का प्रयास करे। अनुच्छेद 51A में एक नया मौलिक कर्तव्य (क्लॉज K) जोड़ा गया, जो माता-पिता या अभिभावकों पर अपने 6-14 वर्ष के बच्चे को शिक्षा के अवसर प्रदान करने का कर्तव्य डालता है। यह संशोधन शिक्षा को मौलिक अधिकार बनाने की दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम था।

question: In which year was the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) initially constituted under the Chairmanship of the Prime Minister of India by an executive order?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: 2005
2010
2007
2008
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2005

Explanation:
The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) was initially constituted by an executive order of the Government of India on 31 May 2005. It was established to formulate policies, plans, and guidelines for disaster management. The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson of NDMA. Later, it was given statutory status under the Disaster Management Act, 2005. NDMA coordinates prevention, preparedness, and mitigation efforts for disasters at the national level.

question: The RTI Act applies to which of the followings in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: Which of the following falls under the Supreme Court’s original jurisdiction, according to the Constitution of India (Article 131)? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Appeals from criminal cases in High Courts
Disputes between States or between a State and the Union
Enforcement of fundamental rights of individuals
Election petitions against sitting Members of Parliaments
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Disputes between States or between a State and the Union

Explanation:
Article 131 of the Indian Constitution confers original jurisdiction on the Supreme Court over disputes between States or between the Centre and States. This includes disputes involving the Government of India and one or more States, or between two or more States. Under this article, the Court hears cases directly, not through appeal. Enforcement of fundamental rights falls under Article 32, election petitions are filed in High Courts, and appeals from criminal cases are under Article 134. Thus, only disputes between States or between a State and the Union come under original jurisdiction. The original jurisdiction is exclusive and covers legal questions involving the interpretation of the Constitution or any other law.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the Council of Ministers at the Union level? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 75
Article 85
Article 74
Article 65
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 74

Explanation:
Article 74 of the Indian Constitution provides for a Council of Ministers at the Union level. It states that there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President. This article establishes the real executive authority in the Council of Ministers. The Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. The interpretation of Article 74 has limited the President's powers, making him bound by the advice of the Council. It is the cornerstone of the parliamentary system, where the actual executive power lies with the Council of Ministers. The 42nd Amendment clarified that the President must act on the advice of the Council, strengthening the cabinet system.

question: The introduction of English education in India was promoted through which of the following documents? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Regulating Act
Pitts India Act
Macaulay’s Minute
Charter Act of 1813
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Macaulay's Minute

Explanation:
The introduction of English education in India was primarily promoted through Macaulay's Minute of 1835. This document, authored by Lord Macaulay, recommended the allocation of government funds for English-medium education rather than traditional Indian languages. Its objective was to create a class of 'Indians in blood and colour, but English in taste and intellect' who would assist in British administration. This policy reshaped the Indian education system, making English the medium of higher education and government jobs. Macaulay's Minute is considered the foundation of modern English education in India.

question: Which of the following is true regarding the tenure and independence of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: The other Election Commissioners can only be removed by the CEC, not by the government.
The CEC’s removal requires assent of the Chief Justice of India but not necessarily the Parliament’s approval.
The CEC enjoys a fixed tenure of ten years and cannot be replaced before that term under any circumstances.
The CEC can only be removed like a Supreme Court judge by a two-thirds majority in Parliament.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The CEC can only be removed like a Supreme Court judge by a two-thirds majority in Parliament.

Explanation:
Under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution, the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) enjoys the same removal procedure as a Supreme Court judge. This means the CEC can be removed only by a special majority of Parliament — a majority of the total membership of each House and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting. This provision ensures the independence of the CEC from executive influence. Other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC. The CEC does not have a fixed tenure; they serve for six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier. The removal does not require the assent of the Chief Justice of India. Thus, the correct statement is that the CEC can only be removed like a Supreme Court judge by a two-thirds majority in Parliament.

Explanation:

question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act abolished the provision for nominating members from the Anglo-Indian community to the State Legislative Assemblies? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)

solution:

Explanation:
The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 abolished the provision for nominating Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. This amendment was made by amending Article 334, which deals with the duration of reservation. It also extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies until 2030. The Act removed Article 331, which empowered the President to nominate two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha. Additionally, the power of the Governor to nominate an Anglo-Indian member to the State Legislative Assembly under Article 333 was also terminated. This amendment marked the end of a 70-year-old provision that had been in place since the adoption of the Constitution in 1950.

question: What special provision is granted under Article 371J of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)

solution:

Explanation:
Article 371J of the Indian Constitution provides special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region of Karnataka state. This article was added by the 92nd Amendment Act, 2003. It mandates separate budget allocation and reservation for the region's development. A separate development board for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region is constituted to ensure educational and economic progress. This is one of several articles (371, 371A, 371B, 371C, 371D, 371E, 371F, 371G, 371H, 371I, 371J) granting special status to different states. question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of India’s federal system, thereby reflecting its unitary character? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Single citizenship for the entire country
Requirement of some Constitutional Amendments to be ratified by States
An upper house of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) representing the states
Division of powers between the Centre and States
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Single citizenship for the entire country

Explanation:
India's federal system features division of powers between Centre and States, supremacy of the Constitution, independent judiciary, and a bicameral legislature (Rajya Sabha representing states). Some Constitutional amendments require ratification by states, strengthening the federal structure. Single citizenship is a unitary feature as it emphasizes national unity, with no separate state citizenship. Federations like the USA have dual citizenship, while India grants equal rights to all citizens under Articles 5-11. Thus, single citizenship does not reflect federalism but unitary character. The other options—amendment ratification, Rajya Sabha, and division of powers—are federal features.

question: The Eleventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists various subjects. Which level of government are these subjects intended for?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Urban Municipal Corporations
State Governments (State legislative matters)
Panchayati Raj Institutions (village/local level)
Central Government (Union ministries)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Panchayati Raj Institutions (village/local level)

Explanation:
The Eleventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains 29 subjects, which are assigned to Panchayati Raj Institutions. This schedule was added through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, with the aim of strengthening rural local self-government. These subjects include agriculture, animal husbandry, fisheries, education, health, rural housing, drinking water, roads, electricity, poverty alleviation, women and child development, and others. Panchayats have the authority to plan and implement schemes on these subjects. This schedule falls under Part IX of the Constitution. State legislatures may provide for the transfer of these subjects to Panchayats. The 11th Schedule empowers local bodies to function as institutions of self-government.

question: What did the Supreme Court decide in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) about the powers of Parliament to amend the Constitution of India?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: The President of India has the ultimate authority to approve or reject constitutional amendments independently.
The Parliament cannot amend any part of the Constitution under any circumstances.
The Parliament can amend the Constitution, but it cannot change or destroy its basic structure or essential features.
The Parliament has unlimited power to amend any part of the Constitution, including the Fundamental Rights.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Parliament can amend the Constitution, but it cannot change or destroy its basic structure or essential features.

Explanation:
In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court propounded the Basic Structure Doctrine. The Court held that while Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution, it cannot destroy or alter its basic structure. The basic structure includes supremacy of the Constitution, rule of law, separation of powers, judicial review, secularism, federalism, and fundamental rights. This ruling limited Parliament's amending power and empowered the judiciary to review constitutional amendments. The doctrine safeguards the democratic and essential features of the Indian Constitution.

question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court uphold the Right to Privacy as a Fundamental Right in 2017? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Shreya Singhal vs. Union of India
Indira Sawhney vs. Union of India
Puttaswamy vs. Union of India
Navtej Singh Johar vs. Union of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Puttaswamy vs. Union of India

Explanation:
The Supreme Court, in a landmark judgment on August 24, 2017, in Puttaswamy vs. Union of India, declared the Right to Privacy as a Fundamental Right under the Constitution. A 9-judge bench unanimously held that privacy is an intrinsic part of Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty). This decision overruled previous judgments that did not recognize privacy as a fundamental right. The ruling established privacy as a constitutionally protected right, limiting state intrusion. This case later influenced the verdict on the Aadhaar scheme and the decriminalization of homosexuality. The judgment emphasized that privacy is essential for human dignity and personal autonomy.

question: Which of the following Committees is a Standing Committee of the Parliament? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Delimitation Commission
Joint Parliamentary Committee on 2G Spectrum
Select Committee on a Bill
Public Accounts Committee
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Public Accounts Committee

Explanation:
The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) is a Standing Committee of Parliament, established in 1921 under the Government of India Act 1919. It examines the annual audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India. The PAC consists of 22 members: 15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha. The Chairman is appointed by the Speaker of Lok Sabha, and by convention, the Chairman is from the opposition party. Other options like Delimitation Commission are not a permanent body, while Joint Parliamentary Committee on 2G Spectrum and Select Committee on a Bill are ad hoc committees. Standing Committees are permanent and constituted every year or periodically.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Total members in PAC → 22
☛ Chairman of PAC is appointed by → Speaker of Lok Sabha
☛ Year of establishment of PAC → 1921
☛ Total Standing Committees in Parliament → 24
☛ PAC examines reports of → CAG

question: Which constitutional Articles ensure the writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and High Courts for enforcing fundamental rights, including RTI? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Articles 51 and 356
Articles 14 and 15
Articles 21 and 39
Articles 32 and 226
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Articles 32 and 226

Explanation:
Under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court has the power to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights, and it is described as the soul of the Constitution. Similarly, Article 226 empowers the High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and other legal rights. These articles include five types of writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari. The Right to Information (RTI) is also protected as a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(a), so these articles are applicable for its enforcement as well.

☛ Which Article is called the soul of the Constitution? → Article 32
☛ How many types of writs can be issued? → 5 types
☛ Under which fundamental right does RTI fall? → Article 19(1)(a)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 32 के तहत सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन हेतु रिट जारी करने का अधिकार है, जिसे संविधान की आत्मा कहा गया है। इसी प्रकार, अनुच्छेद 226 उच्च न्यायालयों को मौलिक अधिकारों और अन्य कानूनी अधिकारों के उल्लंघन पर रिट जारी करने का व्यापक क्षेत्राधिकार प्रदान करता है। इन अनुच्छेदों में बन्दी प्रत्यक्षीकरण (हैबियस कॉर्पस), परमादेश (मैंडेमस), प्रतिषेध (प्रोहिबिशन), अधिकार पृच्छा (क्वो-वारंटो) और उत्प्रेषण (सर्टियोरारी) पांच प्रकार के रिट शामिल हैं। सूचना का अधिकार (RTI) भी मौलिक अधिकार के रूप में अनुच्छेद 19(1)(क) के अंतर्गत संरक्षित है, अतः इसे लागू कराने के लिए भी ये अनुच्छेद उपयोगी हैं।

question: The introduction of English education in India was promoted through which of the following documents? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Charter Act of 1813
Regulating Act
Macaulay’s Minute
Pitts India Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Macaulay's Minute

Explanation:
The introduction of English education in India was primarily promoted through Macaulay's Minute of 1835. Lord Macaulay, a member of the Executive Council under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck, advocated for the adoption of Western education in the Indian education system. His proposal was accepted, and the government decided to make English the medium of instruction. The objective was to create a class of Indians who would be 'Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste, opinions, morals, and intellect.' While the Charter Act of 1813 allocated funds for education, Macaulay's Minute formally pushed for English education. This decision had a lasting impact on India's educational landscape.

☛ Earlier act that allocated funds for education → Charter Act of 1813

भारत में अंग्रेजी शिक्षा की शुरुआत को मुख्य रूप से मैकाले के मिनट (1835) के माध्यम से बढ़ावा दिया गया था। लॉर्ड मैकाले, जो तत्कालीन गवर्नर जनरल लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिंक की कार्यकारी परिषद के सदस्य थे, ने भारतीय शिक्षा प्रणाली में पश्चिमी शिक्षा को अपनाने की वकालत की। उनके प्रस्ताव को स्वीकार करते हुए, सरकार ने अंग्रेजी को शिक्षा का माध्यम बनाने का निर्णय लिया। इस नीति का उद्देश्य 'भारतीयों का एक वर्ग तैयार करना था जो रक्त और रंग में भारतीय हों, लेकिन स्वाद, राय, नैतिकता और बुद्धि में अंग्रेजी हों।' 1813 का चार्टर अधिनियम ने भारत में शिक्षा के लिए धन आवंटित किया, लेकिन अंग्रेजी शिक्षा को आधिकारिक रूप से बढ़ावा देने का श्रेय मैकाले के मिनट को जाता है।
